bib.title: Emerging Properties in Self-Supervised Vision Transformers

read.skipped: Text lines after ~3400 are ImageNet class labels of Fig 11 (t-SNE); skimmed. References skimmed.

question: Does self-supervised pretraining give Vision Transformers properties, such as explicit scene layout and strong k-NN features, that supervised ViTs and convnets lack?
hypothesis: The muted success of ViTs may be explained by supervised pretraining; self-supervised pretraining (as in NLP) should yield distinctive features.
contributions: Observe that self-supervised ViT features contain explicit semantic segmentation information and are excellent k-NN classifiers
Show importance of momentum encoder, multi-crop training and small patches
DINO: self-distillation with no labels, centering and sharpening to avoid collapse
80.1% top-1 linear on ImageNet with ViT-Base

method.summary: DINO trains a student ViT or ResNet to match the output of a momentum (EMA) teacher of identical architecture, using cross-entropy over K-dim softmax outputs, with local-to-global multi-crop views and teacher centering plus sharpening to avoid collapse. Pretrained on ImageNet without labels; evaluated by linear probe, 20-NN, retrieval, copy detection, DAVIS and finetuning.

datasets.name: ImageNet-1k (no labels)
datasets.preprocessing: BYOL augmentations (color jitter, Gaussian blur, solarization) and multi-crop with bicubic interpolation of position embeddings

datasets.name: Revisited Oxford and Paris; INRIA Copydays strong (+10k YFCC100M distractors, 20K YFCC100M for whitening); DAVIS 2017; PASCAL VOC12; CIFAR10/100, iNat18/19, Flowers, Cars

training.objective: cross-entropy H(Pt,Ps) between centered+sharpened teacher and student softmax outputs; 2 global (224^2) views to teacher, all views to student
training.lr_schedule: linear warmup then cosine; weight decay cosine 0.04 to 0.4; teacher momentum cosine 0.996 to 1
training.warmup: 10 epochs (lr); teacher temperature 0.04 to 0.07 linear over first 30 epochs
training.hardware: two 8-GPU machines for ViT-S/16 timing; V100 for throughput
training.compute: 72.6h for 300 epochs 2x224+10x96 ViT-S/16 on two 8-GPU servers; 15.4G peak memory per GPU

other.projection head: 3-layer MLP hidden 2048 GELU, l2-norm bottleneck d=256, weight-normalized linear to K, no BN
other.local crops: 96^2, scale (0.05,s), global (s,1) with s about 0.3; basic setting 2 global + local views, ablations use 6 or 10

inference.samples: single runs; no seeds or error bars reported

parameters.k-NN: k=20, weighted vote, tau=0.07, CLS token
parameters.linear eval: SGD, batch 1024, 100 epochs, no weight decay, lr swept, last 4 CLS tokens concatenated for ViT-S (77.0), final layer + avgpooled patches for ViT-B (78.2)
parameters.segmentation mask: threshold self-attention to keep 60% of mass (Fig 4) or 80% (App. D)

metrics.name: top-1
metrics.definition: ImageNet val accuracy, linear or 20-NN on frozen features

metrics.definition: revisited Oxford/Paris Medium and Hard; Copydays strong

metrics.name: (J&F)m
metrics.definition: DAVIS 2017 mean region similarity and contour accuracy

metrics.name: Jaccard similarity
metrics.definition: between ground truth and mask from thresholded self-attention, PASCAL VOC12 val

limits: Most ablations use ViT-S/16 for 300 epochs and k-NN, not the headline ViT-B/8
No seeds or error bars; authors note linear/finetune evals vary with learning rate

Mask threshold 60% vs 80% inconsistency between Fig 4 and App. D
Authors say multi-crop does not combine with BYOL out of the box and leave it open
Segmentation emergence is shared across self-supervised methods, not DINO specific
Pretraining only on curated ImageNet; uncurated data left to future work
